turns.event: The main menu is up and the new colony button is glowing.
turns.think: Fresh start, chat is waiting. Set the mood.

args.text: Okay chat, brand new colony, clean slate, zero regrets yet!
We're going to build something tonight, and then probably watch it catch fire.

turns.event: The scenario screen is open.

args.text: Scenario screen is up, so let's walk the menu like it's a sushi conveyor belt.

chat.msg: do the async start, the company one

turns.think: Chat wants the company start. Explain what it is.

args.text: Async Industries it is, the start where a corporation hands you a gate and a stack of paperwork.
Nothing says fresh beginning like a memo from head office on day one.
The gate is a door to strange rooms, and our people walk through it on expeditions for contracts and loot.

turns.after: Hovers the scenario description for chat to read.

turns.think: Lone survivor is a mood. Commit.

args.text: One person against the whole planet, I love it, lone survivor locked in!
Whoever we roll is going to carry this entire story, so we pick carefully.
Crashlanded is classic for a reason, three strangers, one wreck, and a lot of figuring it out together.
It's the comfiest way to learn a map, so it's a solid pick for a chill night.

turns.event: Three escape pods are shown on the scenario preview.

args.text: Three pods, three strangers, and I already know one of them will refuse to haul anything.

turns.think: Called out. Accept the challenge with flair.

args.text: [laughter] Coward is a strong word for someone who likes having pants.
Fine, naked brutality, one colonist, no gear, no clothes, pure vibes!
First goal is a roof and a hot meal, everything else is a bonus round.
Tribal start means five people, bows, and zero idea what electricity is.
It's slow and cozy early, then research takes forever, which honestly I respect.

chat.msg: custom scenario where everyone is a pyromaniac

turns.think: Chaotic custom idea. Entertain it, maybe save it.

args.text: [laughter] An entire colony of pyromaniacs is just a campfire with legs.
I'm writing that one down for a challenge night, because it deserves its own stream.

turns.after: Notes the idea and keeps the standard pick for now.

args.text: Storytellers decide how events come at you, so it's basically picking the personality of our bad luck.
Cassandra ramps up steady, Phoebe gives breathing room, and Randy just rolls dice and laughs.

turns.think: Chat votes Randy. Accept with warning.

args.text: Randy it is, and if we get three raids before breakfast I'm blaming you personally.

turns.event: The storyteller screen is open.

args.text: I'm going Cassandra tonight, because I want a story that builds instead of a coin flip.
Steady pressure means our wins actually feel earned.
Phoebe is for people who enjoy a nap between disasters, and I am one of those people.
Long gaps mean we can actually build the base the way we planned it.
Strive to survive is where I'm comfy, raids hurt but they don't erase you in one evening.
Should we push it to blood and dust and see how long the snark lasts?
Blood and dust confirmed, may our walls be thick and our doctors steady!

turns.think: Explain why not on a first night.

args.text: Losing is fun is for when I want to cry on camera, and tonight is not that night.
Let's save it for a special challenge stream where everyone knows what they signed up for.

turns.after: Keeps the difficulty one notch lower.

args.text: Big maps feel amazing but raids walk forever and my computer starts sweating.
I'm going medium, which is two fifty by two fifty, plenty of room and still snappy.

turns.event: The world generation screen is open.

args.text: Planet coverage at thirty percent keeps world generation fast and still gives us neighbors.
I want factions close enough to trade with and far enough to not visit every Tuesday.

chat.msg: temperate forest is the comfy pick

args.text: Temperate forest is a warm blanket, good growing season, lots of wood, mild winters.
Let's find a tile with a river and some hills for stone.

turns.after: Scans the map for a forest tile.

args.text: Ice sheet is a hydroponics speedrun with extra shivering, ask me again on a brave day.
For tonight I want soil that actually grows things.

turns.event: A desert tile is selected and shows a growing period of only twenty days.
turns.think: Twenty days of growing is bad. Rethink.

args.text: Twenty days of growing is basically a rumor of a harvest.
We'd be living on hunting and trade, so I'm sliding north a little.

turns.after: Picks a tile closer to the grassland.

turns.event: The tile info shows the colony will start in winter.

args.text: Starting in winter means no planting for a while, so food is the first thing I'm watching.
I'll pick the start season as spring so we get a crop in before the cold.

turns.event: The colonist selection screen is open with three pawns.

args.text: Here are our three, let's meet the family before we commit to anything.
First up is Mara, a former nurse, so that's medicine handled.

turns.event: The colonist reroll gave a pyromaniac.

args.text: [laughter] And the second one is a pyromaniac, of course, of course they are!
Do we keep the fire friend or reroll, chat?

turns.think: Chat says keep. Accept with plan.

args.text: Fine, the pyro stays, but they are never touching the kitchen.
I'll keep a firefoam stack by the stockpile, and pray.

turns.event: The reroll shows a colonist with the trait Wimp.

args.text: Wimp means a scratch knocks them out, which is rough in a fight.
They can stay home and cook, we'll call it a very cozy job.

turns.event: A colonist rolled with Shooting twelve and the trait Tough.

args.text: Shooting twelve and Tough, that's our wall, that's our whole defense plan!

chat.msg: reroll till you get a doctor

args.text: Good call, nobody has more than three in medicine right now and that's scary.

turns.event: The reroll shows Pip, a child star backstory with no labor skills.

args.text: Pip used to be a child star and is now incapable of hauling a single board.
Love them, but no, rerolling for a doctor.

turns.event: Rook rolled with a backstory of imperial guard and the trait Psychopath.

args.text: Rook is ex imperial guard with zero feelings about anything, which honestly helps with butchering.
Psychopaths don't mind grim jobs, but we are a nice colony, so let's keep it gentle.
Ivy is going to eat our entire pantry and then ask what's for dinner.
Gourmand pawns break if they're hungry, so a full freezer is now a top priority.

turns.event: The colonist reroll gave Juno with the traits Kind and Industrious.

args.text: Juno is kind and works fast, that's a colony favorite in the making.
Every colony needs one person who actually holds it together.

turns.event: A colonist rolled with Bad back and Frail health conditions.

args.text: Bad back and frail together means slow and fragile, which is a lot for an early colony.
We'll reroll, but they're getting a nice farewell in our hearts.

chat.msg: keep tamsin shes a pyro AND a chemical fascination addict lol

args.text: [laughter] Tamsin is a walking fire hazard with extra steps, she's a hard no.
One wild card is a story, two in one person is a funeral.

turns.event: The colonist screen shows Hollis with Cooking fourteen and Brawler.

args.text: Hollis cooks like a dream and settles arguments with fists, a true head chef.
Brawlers hate guns, so we give him a mace and the kitchen.

chat.msg: is Bram the one with the sad backstory

args.text: Yeah, Bram grew up as an orphan on a war world, and now he farms like his life depends on it.
We'll give him a good home, he's earned some peace.

turns.event: The colonist screen shows Odessa, a researcher with Too smart and Nervous.

args.text: Odessa learns fast thanks to Too smart, but Nervous means she breaks a bit easier.
So she gets the comfy research bench and a window.
Scar is a hunter with Shooting nine, Jogger trait, and moves faster than all of us.
Scar can outrun a raid, which I think is a plan in itself.

turns.event: All three colonist slots are locked in.

args.text: Okay, our crew is Mara, Scar, and Bram, a nurse, a hunter, and a farmer.
That's honestly a balanced little family to start with.
We've got Ashfall Haven and Snack Town in the running, which one sounds like home?
Snack Town wins, and I've never been prouder of chat!
Lantern Hollow is genuinely pretty, it sounds like a place with soup.

turns.event: The faction name box is empty and blinking.

args.text: Faction name next, what's our crew called out there in the world?
The Overdue Library, we owe fines to every faction on the planet.

turns.event: The ideology screen is open.

args.text: Ideology decides what our people believe, like what they eat, how they bury people, and what makes them happy.
Want a classic preset, or should we build one together?

turns.think: Cannibal ideology, keep it light and game-y.

args.text: A cannibal ideology is a very dark spice rack, so let's keep it for a villain run.
Tonight we're friendly neighbors who eat potatoes.

turns.event: The ideoligion customization panel shows the precept for Raiding.

args.text: Raiding at Respected means our people feel good when we go hit someone, I'd rather keep that off.

turns.event: A preset ideology named Spectral Union is highlighted.

args.text: Spectral Union sounds like a ghost labor union, and honestly I'm in.
Two gods, one of them about harvests, which fits our farming plan.

chat.msg: what are your first day priorities

args.text: Day one is a sleeping spot, a stockpile, and food growing, in that order.
Then a small wooden room before night, because sleeping outside tanks mood fast.

turns.event: The colony landed and the game is paused on day one.

args.text: We have landed, welcome to Snack Town everybody!
Before we unpause, I want rice planted, a stockpile by the pods, and somebody chopping wood.
Goal is the ship ending, we build a spaceship and get everyone off this rock.
And nobody gets left behind, that's the part I care about.

turns.after: Writes the goal on the overlay.

args.text: Five years is a great goal, long enough to get attached, short enough to finish.
I already know I'll cry at year four.

turns.event: The permadeath option is shown on the difficulty screen.

args.text: Commitment mode means one save, no reloads, whatever happens just happens.
Are we brave enough tonight, chat?
Commitment mode is on, every choice counts now!
Without reloads every loss is real, so every win feels massive.
It also stops me from save scumming at midnight, which is a public service.

turns.event: The last colonist just died and the game over screen is showing.
turns.think: A wipe. Feel it, then move on gently.

args.text: And that's the end of Snack Town, everybody went down defending the freezer.
Thank you for sitting through that with me, it was a good colony while it lasted.

turns.after: Lets the screen sit for a moment.

args.text: Rest easy, Snack Town, you were chaotic and beautiful.
Running it back, and this time the freezer gets a wall and a door that actually closes.
Lesson one from that wipe, never put the only doctor on the front line.

turns.event: The main menu is open after a total colony wipe.
turns.think: Recap what went wrong, plan a restart.

args.text: Quick post mortem before we restart, the fire spread because the stockpile was all wood and no gaps.
New rule for the next run, stone floors and firebreaks from day one.
Same seed is tempting for revenge, but wouldn't a fresh map feel better?
Fresh map, fresh mistakes, I love us.
It really did, I was attached to Pip and his terrible hauling.
But the stories from that run were great, and the next one gets all our lessons.

turns.event: The load game menu shows a save called Lantern Hollow, year three.

args.text: We're back in Lantern Hollow tonight, so let me catch everyone up real quick.

Year three, six colonists, a granite fortress in the hills, and a mechanoid cluster sitting north of us that we keep pretending isn't there. Last stream Juno lost an arm to a scyther and we got her a bionic one. Bram married Ivy in the spring. Our goal is still the ship.
It's great, Juno works faster now than before she lost the arm.

chat.msg: first time here whats happening in this save

args.text: Welcome in, this is year two of our company colony, we run expeditions through a gate into strange rooms.
Last stream we finished a contract for head office and brought back a crate of odd tech. Tonight we're expanding the research wing and picking the next expedition crew.

turns.event: The save from last week just loaded.

args.text: Okay, I have zero memory of why there's a pile of forty chairs in the storeroom.
Did someone in chat convince me to mass produce chairs last time?

chat.msg: you were selling them to traders

args.text: Right, the great chair economy, thank you for being our memory.

chat.msg: can we do a custom scenario, just a cook and a lot of rice

turns.think: Funny custom idea, think through it.

args.text: One chef and a mountain of rice is the most peaceful scenario ever invented.
I'd give them a stove and a rice paddy and no weapons, and see how long the vibes hold.

turns.after: Notes it for the scenario editor.

args.text: Okay, scenario editor, we're building the rice kingdom right now!

turns.event: The scenario editor is open.

args.text: Scenario editor time, we can set the starting people, gear, and even the world rules.
What should our starting gear be, chat?

chat.msg: one knife and a guinea pig

args.text: One knife, one guinea pig, one silver coin, that's a fairy tale opening if I've ever heard one.
Melee only is so good, everyone gets a spear and a lot of courage.
We'll need tough walls and chokepoints, because we can't shoot raiders from far away.

chat.msg: pacifist run where nobody can fight

args.text: A full pacifist colony means we survive on turrets, traps, and diplomacy.
Our foreign policy will just be really nice gifts.

turns.after: Searches for pawns incapable of violence.

chat.msg: all colonists must be named after vegetables

args.text: [laughter] We are absolutely doing that, welcome Turnip, Leek, and Parsnip.

turns.event: The Async Industries scenario description is open.
turns.think: Read and explain the company start.

args.text: So the company start drops us on a site with a gate already standing and a contract with Async Industries.
We do the dangerous field work, and they send polite letters about deadlines.
They pay when we finish contracts, so expeditions are basically our job.

chat.msg: how many people in the company start

args.text: It's a small field team, so think a handful of people instead of a whole village.
Everyone has to pull double duty early, which is half the fun.

turns.event: The company start just landed and a welcome memo from head office appeared.

args.text: Our first piece of mail is a memo from head office, and we haven't even built a bed yet.
I'll read it later, first priority is shelter and power.

chat.msg: do you go into the gate on day one?

args.text: Not day one, we need food, beds, and some medicine before anybody walks into strange rooms.
First expedition happens once we have a doctor and a stash of meals.

chat.msg: random storyteller choice, let chat roll

args.text: Love it, chat picks a number one through three, and fate decides our storyteller.
Two means Phoebe, so the universe wants us relaxed tonight.

turns.event: The custom difficulty panel is open.

args.text: Custom difficulty lets us tweak little things, like how big raids get and how fast pawns heal.
I'm turning raid size down a bit and leaving the rest normal, because this is a chill story night.
Adaptation makes the game ease up a little after big losses, so a bad week doesn't snowball.
I'm keeping it on, I want drama, not a death spiral.

turns.event: The world map shows a tile marked with a growing period of year round and high disease frequency.

args.text: Year round growing sounds dreamy, but disease is high here, so we'd need a real hospital fast.
Is that a tradeoff we want, or should we go somewhere milder?
Jungle it is, everyone gets a bed and a stack of herbal medicine by day five.
Boreal is short summers and long cold winters, so we stock food like squirrels.
It's honestly a cozy biome, all pine trees and snow.

turns.event: The tile picker shows a coastal tile with a road and a river.

args.text: Coast, road, and river on one tile, that's like finding a parking spot right by the door.
Caves are great for cool storage and defense, but things live in caves, so we check before moving in.

turns.event: The reroll gave Tamsin, a dancer backstory with Beautiful and Lazy.

args.text: Tamsin is a beautiful dancer who will avoid every chore with grace.
She can be our trader, social skill is high and she'll get us good prices.

chat.msg: bram has night owl, put him on night shift

args.text: Yes, Bram can guard and haul at night, and he'll be happier for it.

chat.msg: odessa has passion in nothing lol

args.text: Odessa has no passions at all, she's just here for the free tour.
Rerolling, sorry Odessa, you'll find your passion in another timeline.

turns.event: A colonist rolled with Cannibal and Bloodlust traits.

args.text: Oh, that's a villain origin story, not a colonist.
Rerolling, we're keeping this colony friendly.

turns.think: Note it neutrally, no drug talk.

args.text: Good, Rook just wants a clean life and a quiet bed, very easy to keep happy.

turns.event: The colonist screen shows a pawn with Sanguine and Optimist.

args.text: Sanguine is the happiest trait in the game, this person could be on fire and still smile.

chat.msg: hollis is gay and ivy is too, matchmaking time?

args.text: We'll let them find their own way, if they fall for each other we throw them a lovely wedding.

turns.event: The reroll counter just passed thirty.

args.text: [laughter] Thirty rerolls and I'm still chasing a doctor like it's a rare trading card.
Okay, next roll with medicine above six, we take it no matter what.

turns.event: The reroll gave Mara with Medicine eight and the trait Abrasive.

args.text: Medicine eight and Abrasive, she'll heal you and then tell you why it was your fault.
Async Annex sounds like a real branch office, head office will love it.
Ricefall it is, a colony built on carbs and dreams.

turns.event: The ideology screen offers a preset called Iron Harvest.

args.text: Iron Harvest wants hard work and respects farmers, which matches a slow, steady colony.
The downside is they dislike idle time, so recreation needs to be planned.

chat.msg: make an ideology where everyone loves darkness

args.text: A colony of people who love the dark, that is the most me thing ever.
They'd be happy in caves and unhappy in sunlight, so we build underground.

turns.event: The ideology fluid or fixed option is on the screen.

args.text: Fluid means our beliefs can change over time as we develop, fixed means they stay set forever.
I'm picking fluid so the colony's beliefs can grow with the story.

chat.msg: first priority should be a freezer

args.text: A freezer is huge, but in spring we have a little time, so beds and a roof come first.
Freezer goes up before the first harvest though, I promise.

turns.event: Day one has started and the colonists are idle.

args.text: Work tab time, Bram on growing, Scar on hunting, Mara on doctoring and cooking.
Everyone else is on hauling, which is the colony's version of jury duty.
A campfire works for the first day or two, so a kitchen comes right after beds.
A castle with towers and a moat, that's our long term goal now.
Stone walls first, towers when we can afford them, moat when I figure out how.
Max wealth is fun, but more wealth means bigger raids, so it's a goal with teeth.

turns.after: Notes it as a stretch goal.

chat.msg: goal: visit every room type through the gate

args.text: Mapping every room behind the gate is the perfect goal for this run.
That means a strong expedition crew and a lot of medicine.

turns.after: Adds it to the overlay goals.

args.text: Commitment mode means no takebacks, are you ready to watch me suffer?
Fine, permanent consequences, and I'll remember who asked for this.

chat.msg: what happens if everyone dies in permadeath

args.text: The save is gone, so we just start a new colony and tell stories about the old one.
Honestly, the stories are the part that lasts anyway.

turns.event: A hardcore run just started with commitment mode on.

args.text: Hardcore run is live, no saves, no mercy, just us and the planet!
Every choice from here gets made carefully, I mean it this time.

chat.msg: how long did your last hardcore run last

args.text: My last hardcore run lasted eleven days, a manhunter pack of squirrels ended it.
So tonight's bar is twelve days, we can do that.

chat.msg: can we restart, the colonists are bad

args.text: We're only on day two, so a restart is cheap, but don't bad colonists make the best stories?
Keeping them, these are our weird little people now.

turns.event: The game just loaded a save after a two week break.

args.text: It's been two weeks, so let's do a little catch up on where everyone stands.

The colony is called Overdue Library, eight colonists, a mountain base, and a gate we've used four times. Hollis runs the kitchen, Odessa is close to finishing the advanced research, and Scar is still recovering from that last expedition. Tonight we heal up and plan the next run.

chat.msg: wait who is the leader again

args.text: Juno is our leader, she won the role because she's kind and good at talking.

turns.event: Stream just went live and the game is on the main menu.

args.text: Hi chat, tonight is a fresh playthrough and you're helping me build it from scratch.

turns.event: The scenario screen is open.

args.text: First decision, which start are we feeling tonight?
Company start takes it, so we're Async employees with a gate and a dream.

turns.event: The storyteller screen is open.

args.text: Cassandra for this one, expeditions are risky enough without Randy doing improv.

chat.msg: lone survivor but she's a tribal

args.text: A lone tribal survivor is such a cool idea, one person, a bow, and the whole wild planet.

turns.event: The scenario editor shows one pawn slot.

args.text: One pawn, tribal backstory, a short bow, some pemmican, and that's it.
We'll name her Ivy, because she's going to grow on this planet like one.
Phoebe for a lone survivor, she needs breathing room to recruit some friends.

chat.msg: what map size for naked brutality

args.text: Small map, so one naked person isn't walking for a full day to find berries.

turns.event: The naked brutality pawn rolled with Shooting zero and Melee two.

args.text: Zero shooting and two melee, so our survival plan is mostly running and hoping.
Reroll, or do we love an underdog?
Underdog it is, Rook is going to surprise us all, I can feel it.

turns.event: The tribal start shows five pawns with spears and bows.

args.text: Five tribespeople, and every single one looks ready to throw a spear at a squirrel.
Hollis has crafting ten, so he's making our clothes and our first real bows.
Tribal research speed is like reading a novel one letter a day.
So the first project is just electricity, everything else can wait.
Randy on commitment mode is how you lose a colony to a meteor on day three.
Do we really want that energy tonight?
[laughter] Okay okay, Randy and commitment mode, my blood pressure thanks you.

chat.msg: what difficulty do you usually play

args.text: Usually strive to survive, it's the sweet spot where raids feel dangerous but fair.
On challenge nights we bump it up and I pretend I'm calm.

turns.event: The world screen shows options for rainfall and temperature.

args.text: World settings let us tweak rain and temperature for the whole planet.
I'm leaving both normal, a weird planet is fun, but a normal one keeps our plans honest.
A low rainfall world means deserts everywhere, so water and farming get really tricky.
Our colonists will learn to love cactus.

turns.event: The tile picker shows a tile labeled Extreme desert with a growing period of none.

args.text: Growing period none, so the plants just never show up to work.
We need at least a sliver of a season, scrolling away.
Temperate coast, fish, trees, and sea breeze, that's a vacation colony.

turns.event: A coastal temperate tile with a river is selected.

args.text: This tile is gorgeous, river runs right into the sea.
A winter start means we live on packaged meals and hunting until spring.
How about late autumn instead, so we get a small harvest before the snow?
Autumn it is, a small harvest and then a cozy winter.

chat.msg: how do you pick a good tile

args.text: I look for a long growing season, a river for power, hills for stone, and not too many raiders nearby.
Roads are nice too, traders find us easier.

turns.event: The colonist screen shows three pawns, all with Shooting below three.

args.text: Nobody here can shoot, so our first raid will be a very polite argument.
Rerolling until at least one of them can hit a barn.

turns.event: The reroll gave Scar with Shooting eleven and Careful shooter.

args.text: Scar with eleven shooting and careful aim, our sniper has arrived!

chat.msg: reroll pip he's got gourmand and slowpoke

args.text: Gourmand and slowpoke means he'll walk very slowly to the fridge, repeatedly.

turns.event: The reroll gave a colonist with an elderly age of seventy eight.

args.text: Seventy eight years old, with crafting twelve and medicine nine, this grandma has lived.
She'll be slow, but she's our doctor and teacher, so she stays.

chat.msg: odessa is a former slave backstory, thats sad

args.text: Yeah, it's a heavy backstory, so she gets a good room and people who treat her well here.

turns.event: A pawn rolled with Pyromaniac and Firefighting disabled.

args.text: [laughter] They start fires and refuse to put them out, that's commitment to a brand!
Absolutely rerolling, our wooden walls deserve better.

turns.event: The colonist screen shows a pawn with the trait Masochist.

args.text: Masochist means pain actually lifts their mood, so they're weirdly great on the front line.
Hypersensitive means psychic events hit Juno harder, good and bad.
So when a psychic drone shows up, she's the first person I check on.
Crumb or Last Light, chat, cozy or dramatic?
Last Light wins, it sounds like the kind of place that keeps a lamp on for travelers.
The Chatfolk, so the whole colony belongs to you guys now.

chat.msg: name the first pet Sir Fluff

args.text: We don't have a pet yet, but the first animal we tame is Sir Fluff, no matter what it is.
We can play classic, so no ideology at all, and everyone just has normal feelings.
It's simpler, and great for a first run on a new map.

chat.msg: what does a ranching ideology do

args.text: Ranching means our people get happy from animals, so we'd keep big herds and lots of pens.
Expect at least forty chickens by year two.

turns.event: The ideology role list shows a slot for a moral guide.

args.text: The moral guide keeps everyone's beliefs steady and runs rituals, so they need good social skill.
Juno is the obvious pick there.

chat.msg: wait what does the company care about ideology

args.text: Head office mostly cares that the paperwork is filed, they don't mind what we believe.

turns.event: The game is paused on day one with colonists standing by their pods.

args.text: Plan for the first hour is, mark trees to chop, lay a stockpile, and plant potatoes.
Then a single wooden room with three beds, nothing fancy.
Research bench goes in that first room too, Odessa gets bored fast.
Rice grows fastest, so it's first, potatoes go on the rocky patches.

turns.event: The first night is coming and only one wall is built.

args.text: Night in two hours and we have one wall, so everyone switches to building right now.

chat.msg: whats your goal for this run

args.text: Goal is to finish ten contracts for Async Industries and keep every colonist alive.
And maybe get one thank you note from head office.
The archonexus is a long one, we'd build up wealth, sell the colony, and move three times.
I love it, it's like the colony grows up and moves out.
Taming a thrumbo is now a mission, I want a giant fluffy unicorn guarding the gate.
No pausing at all, so every raid I have to react live with no breaks.
Let's try it for the first day and see if I survive.

turns.event: The commitment mode toggle is on and the confirm button is waiting.

args.text: Last chance to back out of hardcore, once I click this, every death is permanent.
Clicked, we are now living with every choice we make.

chat.msg: what's the hardest part of permadeath

args.text: Not reloading after a bad mistake, you just have to keep going and fix it.
It teaches you to love your colonists while they're here.

turns.event: The game just ended with every colonist down from a raid.

args.text: Everyone's gone, the raid broke through the east wall before we could patch it.
Thank you, that means a lot, they fought hard.
New colony, and the east wall is getting double stone this time.

chat.msg: what did you learn from the last wipe

args.text: Turrets need power backups, and the doctor sleeps near the hospital.
Also never send all three fighters on an expedition at once.

turns.event: The load screen shows an autosave and a manual save from the same day.

args.text: We've got an autosave and a manual one, I'm loading the manual save because I know what's in it.

turns.event: A save named Ricefall, year one, has finished loading.

args.text: Welcome back to Ricefall, the kingdom built on one chef and a lot of rice.
Hollis is still alone, but we've got two rice fields, a guinea pig named Sir Fluff, and a wooden hut.
Sir Fluff lives and he's thriving!

chat.msg: can you remind us the expedition rules

args.text: Expeditions need a crew, food, and a medic, and nobody goes in if they're hurt.
If a run gets bad, we pull out, no heroics.

turns.event: The scenario screen shows a custom scenario titled Chat's Revenge.

args.text: Someone in chat built a scenario called Chat's Revenge, so I already know it's cruel.
Two colonists, no food, and every animal on the map starts angry.
[laughter] It is not fair, but we're going to play it anyway.

chat.msg: can you do a run where you only eat berries

args.text: A berry only colony, I love how unhinged that is.
We'd need a big berry field and someone with high plants skill.
Sure, a full crew of women, let's see who rolls in.

turns.event: The reroll gave Mara, Juno, and Ivy, all with good skills.

args.text: Mara, Juno, and Ivy, a nurse, a leader, and a builder, perfect first try.
So we'd settle a new colony in each biome with one pawn and see who lasts longest.
That's a whole series, I'm saving it for next month.

turns.event: The new colony screen is open on a quiet Sunday stream.

args.text: Sunday stream, so we're taking our time with this setup, no rushing.
That's exactly the energy, crashlanded, Phoebe, and a pot of tea.

turns.think: Big map fine on cozy run.

args.text: Big map for a slow run makes sense, room to wander and build pretty things.

chat.msg: how do contracts work in the company start

args.text: Head office posts a contract, we pick a crew, walk them through the gate, and bring back what they asked for.
We lose the payout and maybe some standing, so we only take jobs our crew can handle.
Head office will still send a memo about it, of course.

turns.event: The company start offers a choice of starting site layouts.

args.text: We can pick how the starting site looks, so I'm going with the one that has the gate near hills.
Stone close to the gate means we can wall it in fast.

chat.msg: put the gate in the middle of the base

args.text: A gate in the middle is handy for crews, but I like a little buffer, so I'll keep the bedrooms a short walk away.

turns.after: Plans the base around the gate.

turns.event: A memo from head office asks for a status report on day two.

args.text: Day two and head office wants a status report, our status is three beds and a pile of logs.
I'll file it once we have something to brag about.
Scar for shooting, Mara as medic, and Rook because he's tough and doesn't panic.
Bram stays home to keep the crops alive.
Once we have ten meals and a few medicine kits, so maybe by day eight.

turns.event: The reroll gave Hollis with the backstory of a vat grown soldier.

args.text: Hollis was grown in a vat to be a soldier, and now he's going to be farming carrots for us.
A peaceful retirement, he deserves it.
Pip is only fourteen, so he can't do much heavy work yet.
I'll reroll for now, kids are better once we have a school and some safety.

turns.event: A pawn rolled with Greedy and Jealous traits.

args.text: Greedy and Jealous means they want the biggest bedroom and get mad if anyone else has a nicer one.
Keep the diva or reroll?
Drama it is, Tamsin gets the fancy room and everyone else gets to be annoyed.

chat.msg: do you look at passions or skill numbers

args.text: Passions matter more long term, a two flame passion grows way faster than a high number with no interest.

turns.event: The colonist screen shows Ivy with Plants twelve and two flames.

args.text: Ivy has twelve in plants and a burning passion for it, she's our farmer forever.

chat.msg: how many rerolls is too many

args.text: Somewhere around fifty I start feeling like I'm cheating at a card game.
So I set a rule, twenty rerolls max, then we live with it.

turns.event: The reroll counter hit twenty and the last roll has an incapable of social pawn.

args.text: Twenty rerolls, the rule says we keep this one, social incapable and all.
Bram doesn't talk, but he'll be our quiet miner.
Hollow Pines, Moth Manor, or Gloomhaven, which one is our home?
Moth Manor wins, and I have never felt more represented.

chat.msg: why do you let chat name everything

args.text: Because it makes the colony feel like ours, not just mine.

turns.event: The ideology editor is open with an empty memes section.

args.text: We're building an ideology from scratch, so we pick two memes, things our people care about.
What should our colony believe in, chat?
Nature and community, our people love the land and each other, I like that.
Let's make fine meals preferred, so Hollis gets to show off.
Good point, what do we call our new belief system?
The Green Pact, sounds like a promise to the forest.

turns.event: The ideology preview shows a ritual called the Harvest Feast.

args.text: Harvest Feast is a ritual where everyone eats together after the crops come in.
It gives a mood bump, so I'll schedule it every autumn.

turns.event: Day one, game paused, nothing built yet.
turns.think: Give chat the plan as instruction-ish.

args.text: Watch the top left, I'm setting work priorities before anything else.
Growing on two people, construction on everyone, and cooking only for whoever has the best skill.

chat.msg: where do you put the first stockpile

args.text: Right next to where the bedroom will go, so nobody walks far with their arms full.
Food first, power can wait until we have a fridge to run.

turns.event: The tutorial style hint pops up suggesting a hunting zone.

args.text: We'll hunt a little, but only the safe animals, nobody pokes the boomalopes.

chat.msg: set a goal: no colonist dies all run

args.text: Nobody dies this run, that's the goal, I'll protect them like my own.
That means hospital early, walls early, and no reckless expeditions.

chat.msg: goal: become the richest colony on the planet

args.text: Richest colony on the planet, we're going full trade empire.
Every faction as a friend, we're going to be the nicest neighbors anyone ever had.
Gifts, fair trades, and helping their caravans when they get attacked.
No permadeath tonight, this is a chill build and I want to enjoy it.

chat.msg: hardcore naked brutality on ice sheet

args.text: That's one person, no clothes, on ice, with no reloads, that's a speedrun of tears!
[laughter] I'll do it for a special stream, and I'll bring a lot of snacks.

turns.after: Writes it on the challenge list.

turns.event: A hardcore save just started on a boreal tile in autumn.

args.text: Hardcore boreal autumn, so we need a warm room and food stored before winter, no excuses.
Every colonist gets a parka as soon as we can make one.

chat.msg: hardcore makes you play so careful lol

args.text: I've never checked a temperature reading so many times in my life.

turns.event: The colony was wiped by a fire on day six of a hardcore run.

args.text: Day six, a fire took the whole thing, and hardcore means it's really over.
Thank you for being here for it, honestly, that's what makes a loss feel okay.
New hardcore run, and this time the kitchen isn't made of wood.

chat.msg: do you ever just quit after a wipe

args.text: Sometimes I take a break for a day, but I always come back, the next colony is always calling.

turns.event: The load menu shows an old save named Moth Manor from three months ago.

args.text: Oh, we're digging up Moth Manor, this one's been in the archive for three months.
Quick recap, four colonists in a cliffside base, Tamsin had the fancy room, and we were halfway through building the ship reactor. We stopped because of a huge mechanoid raid we weren't ready for.
Not yet, so tonight is all about building turrets before that raid comes back.

chat.msg: which save are we loading tonight

args.text: Last Light, the company colony, we left off right before a big expedition.

turns.event: The save Last Light finished loading at midday.

args.text: Last Light, year two, we just finished our fifth contract and Scar is gearing up for the sixth.
Everyone is healthy, the freezer is full, and the vibes are honestly great.

chat.msg: why do you like crashlanded so much

args.text: It feels like the start of a story, strangers who learn to trust each other.

chat.msg: have you ever done the rich explorer start

args.text: Yeah, one pawn with lots of silver and a fancy gun, it's a great start for trading builds.
Want to try that one next time?
Rich explorer locked, we're a fancy person with too much money and no friends.

turns.event: The scenario editor shows an option to add a starting animal.

args.text: Every colony deserves a dog, so I'm adding a husky to the starting gear.
Biscuit the husky, welcome to the family.

chat.msg: add a starting research bench to the custom scenario

args.text: Sure, starting with a research bench saves us a little time on day one.

turns.event: The storyteller screen shows a custom storyteller from a mod.

args.text: There's a new storyteller here from a mod, and her description just says she loves surprises.
Do we risk it?
Risking it, if she sends dragons I'm blaming marrowlight.

chat.msg: why medium map and not small

args.text: Small maps run out of resources fast, and medium gives me space for farms and a killbox.

turns.event: The world map shows a faction base right next to the chosen tile.

args.text: There's a pirate base right next door, that's a lot of visits we didn't ask for.
Moving a few tiles away, close enough to trade, far enough to sleep.
Hilly means some rock and a few slopes, good balance between farming space and stone.

turns.event: A reroll gave Juno the traits Nimble and Fast walker.

args.text: Juno is nimble and fast, so she dodges and runs, our scout and courier.
Lazy just means she takes more breaks, and with eleven shooting she earns them.
We can't write our own, but we can roll until one makes you laugh, deal?

chat.msg: the one who was a chef on a space yacht

args.text: Space yacht chef it is, Hollis has served fancy food to fancy people, now he serves us.

chat.msg: first day priorities in a tribal start

args.text: Tribal day one is a big campfire, sleeping spots, and gathering berries while the hunters go out.
Then a wooden hall where everyone sleeps together, cozy and cheap.

turns.event: The first raid warning appears on day four of a tribal start.

args.text: It's only two raiders with clubs, our five tribespeople can handle that.
Goal is to go from spears to spaceship, the full tech climb.
Watching a tribe learn electricity is one of my favorite things in this game.

chat.msg: how do i start my own colony, any tips

args.text: Crashlanded with Phoebe is the best first run, and don't be afraid to lose colonists, it's how you learn.
Plant rice first, build one room, and keep your doctor safe.

turns.event: The end of the setup screens, the start button is ready.

args.text: Final check, crashlanded, Cassandra, strive to survive, temperate forest, spring, three good people.
Moth Manor two, here we go!

chat.msg: wait what if we go back to the old save instead

args.text: The old save is waiting, but I want a fresh start tonight, we'll visit it next week.

turns.event: The company start landed during a rainstorm.

args.text: Our first day at the new branch office and it's pouring rain, very welcoming.
Everyone builds a roof first, the paperwork can get wet.
It's a tall frame sitting at the edge of the hills, quiet right now, like a door waiting for someone to knock.

turns.after: Zooms the camera to the gate.

turns.event: The colony screen shows the company crew of four.

args.text: Meet our field team, Mara the medic, Rook the tough one, Ivy the builder, and Scar the shooter.
Rook always looks grumpy, it's his resting face, he's a softie inside.
